promptLatex: To prove 'a number is even if and only if it is divisible by 2', which proof strategy is most appropriate?
choices: both directions of the biconditional separately
answerLatex: both directions of the biconditional separately
hintLatex: A biconditional 'P iff Q' requires proving two directions: P implies Q, and Q implies P.
One direction usually needs factoring and the other needs substitution, and they are not the same argument run backwards.
Prove each direction under separate headings before finishing.
solutionLatex:
Proof of the biconditional requires two separate directions:

Forward direction (if even then divisible by 2): By definition, an even number is 2k for some integer k, so it is divisible by 2.

Reverse direction (if divisible by 2 then even): If n is divisible by 2, then n = 2k for some integer k, so by definition n is even.

Both directions are proved independently and the biconditional is established.
